findings.bug: Sizes the buffer with in.available() and does a single in.read(data) whose return value is ignored, so any stream where available() underreports or read() returns fewer bytes than requested yields a truncated/zero-padded, hence corrupted, Base64 result.
findings.why_real: InputStream Javadoc: available() is only an estimate of bytes that can be read without blocking (not the total length) and read(byte[]) reads 'up to' the array length and may read fewer bytes; correct code must loop until EOF (e.g. IOUtils.toByteArray/readAllBytes). The unused return value of read() proves the missing loop.
findings.how_to_prove: Wrap the image bytes in an InputStream whose read(byte[]) returns 1 byte per call (or whose available() reports fewer than the total). Expected: Base64 of the full image. Actual: buffer sized to the first available() value with only 1 byte filled and the rest left as 0x00, producing a wrong/truncated Base64 string.

findings.bug: The lock advertises reentrancy (支持重入) but keeps no hold count: tryLock() returns true again when the thread already holds the key, yet the first unlock() unconditionally DELs the key, so a single unlock releases a lock that was acquired multiple times.
findings.why_real: The class Javadoc states '支持重入' (supports reentrancy). A reentrant Lock must require as many unlock() calls as lock()/tryLock() successes (java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock contract). Here there is no counter; unlock() runs the DEL script on the first call and removes the ThreadLocal, breaking that contract.
findings.how_to_prove: With a mock StringRedisTemplate: thread A calls tryLock() (true), calls tryLock() again reentrantly (true), then unlock() once. Expected: A still holds the lock (a second thread's tryLock() must return false). Actual: the key is deleted after one unlock(), so another thread's tryLock() succeeds while A still believes it holds the lock.
